title: Pricing & Billing Request Priority Scorecard and Routing Guide
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Customers and account teams submit a steady stream of non-bug requests about pricing commitments, invoicing behaviors, cost allocation for marketplace sales, and one-off billing setups. Currently triage is adhoc: requests land in shared inboxes or Slack, causing slow routing, inconsistent responses, and repeated follow-ups from Sales and Finance.

Goal:
Create a lightweight, repeatable scoring system and routing guide (the Scorecard) that Product, Sales, Finance, and Pricing Ops can use to: 1) prioritize incoming pricing/billing requests, 2) route them to the right owner (Pricing Ops / Finance / Enterprise PM / Solutions Engineering / Backlog), and 3) set SLAs and handoff artefacts. This should reduce cycle time to first response, standardize decisions on commitment approvals, and surface trends for roadmap decisions.

Scope (in scope):
- New commitment terms and custom pricing requests from customers or partners
- Invoicing exceptions and technical invoice formatting requests that require product or billing-engine changes
- Requests to change marketplace revenue allocation or introduce new marketplace fee flows
- Requests for cost allocation tooling (per team, per product) that affect UI/console exports or billing pipelines

Out of scope:
- Individual bug reports or system outages (continue to use incident/bug flow)
- Standard self-serve pricing page feedback that does not request commitment or invoice changes

Scorecard design (proposed):
Each incoming request is scored across five dimensions (0-5 each). Weights are applied to compute a weighted score (0-100). The scoring sheet is a simple checklist that can be completed by the intake owner in under 10 minutes.
- Revenue / ARR impact (weight 35): estimates change in ARR or committed dollars if implemented (0 none — 5 > $1M / year)
- Time to Close / Sales urgency (weight 20): impact to outstanding deal closures or renewals (0 no impact — 5 blocks multiple PRs)
- Legal / Compliance risk (weight 15): does request have regulatory constraints or contractual obligations (0 none — 5 blocks go-live)
- Implementation complexity (weight 15): product + infra effort (0 trivial config — 5 cross-team multi-sprint)
- Long-term product value (weight 15): likely recurring value to customers/product (0 one-off — 5 platform-level capability)

Routing thresholds (examples):
- Score >= 70: Escalate to Pricing Review Committee (Pricing Ops + Finance + PM) and schedule 48h intake call; owner: Pricing Ops.
- Score 40-69: Route to Enterprise PM + Solutions Engineering for scoping; owner: Enterprise PM, review in weekly intake sync.
- Score 20-39: Routed to Product Backlog with estimated T-shirt size; owner: Product Manager for backlog scheduling.
- Score <20: Send templated response with self-serve guidance and close after 7 days if no escalation.

Routing examples (concrete):
- Custom multi-year commitment with $800k ARR impact and legal SLA modifications: revenue=4 (140), urgency=4 (80), legal=3 (45), complexity=3 (45), product value=3 (45) => weighted score 355/5 => normalized 71 -> escalate to Pricing Review Committee.
- Request to change line-item label on invoice for a single customer (low revenue, low risk): scores produce normalized 15 -> templated response + backlog if requested.

Process & SLAs:
- Intake owner (initially Pricing Ops) triages new tickets within 48 business hours and completes the scorecard.
- Triage committee meets weekly (1 hour) to adjudicate 40-70 band items and fast-track >=70 items within 72 hours.
- For escalations, owner documents decision in the ticket with links to required artifacts: GH issue or PR, revised contract language (Drive/Confluence), Finance ticket for invoicing pipeline changes.

Ticket artefacts required when routing to Engineering or Finance:
- Acceptance criteria (explicit): example invoice with fields, contract amendment snippet, or a rollout plan for commitment billing.
- Implementation estimate (engineering points or calendar estimate).
- Data/export sample: example invoice lines or sample CSV for cost allocation changes.

Governance & metrics to track success:
- Mean time to first response (target <48 hours)
- Median time from intake to decision for >=70 items (target <72 hours)
- % of routed items with complete artefacts at handoff (target >90%)
- Trend dashboard for request categories (commitments | invoicing | marketplace | allocation) to inform roadmap decisions

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket):
- A templated scorecard Google Sheet and scoring instructions are published in Confluence with links from Intake form.
- Intake form (Zendesk/Form) updated to require minimum fields for scoring (estimated ARR, customer impact note, legal flag).
- Routing automation rules drafted (Zapier/works / internal automation) that apply thresholds and assign to the appropriate team queue.
- Weekly triage cadence and meeting invite created; first two meetings scheduled and owners confirmed.
- Pilot with 4 live customer requests representing each category completed and outcomes documented.

Next steps and open questions:
- Should Pricing Ops remain the intake owner long-term or rotate between PM/Finance? (P1 decision)
- Which system will store final decisions and artifacts as single source of truth? Proposal: Confluence + ticket link.
- Do we need a billing-engine feature flag to support quick toggles for invoicing exceptions? Coordinate with Infra/ENG.

Deliverables (links):
- Draft Scorecard template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/scorecard-draft
- Confluence intake doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/enterprise-billing-intake
- Example GH PR for invoice-formatting change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pricing/pull/402
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/enterprise-billing/triage-dashboard

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sales bypasses the scorecard for high-pressure deals -> Mitigation: require Sales Ops approval stamp for any manual bypass and log in dashboard.
- Risk: Scorecard weights misaligned with actual business impact -> Mitigation: review weights monthly during pilot and adjust with data.

Stakeholders to consult:
- Pricing Ops (primary), Finance, Legal, Enterprise Sales, Solutions Engineering, Billing Engineering, Product Analytics
